subject: history_social
passage: Trams have run through the streets of Kolkata, India, since 1873, when the first cars were pulled by horses along a short route between Sealdah and Armenian Ghat. The system was electrified in 1902 and at its height carried passengers across much of the city. The network that survives after decades of closures and the removal of tracks from many of the city's busiest ______ the oldest operating tram system in Asia and the last one in India. Supporters argue that the trams, which produce no exhaust, deserve new investment rather than gradual retirement.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the third sentence is "The network," and everything from "that survives" to "busiest streets" is a clause that identifies which network. The verb is "is." No punctuation may separate a subject from its verb, however long the subject is.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A comma between the subject "The network …" and its verb "is" breaks the rule that nothing separates a subject from its verb.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A semicolon must join two independent clauses; "is the oldest operating tram system" has no subject of its own.
explanation.C: Correct. The long subject connects directly to its verb "is" with no punctuation in between.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A single dash here would cut the subject off from its verb; dashes set off extra information, but "is the oldest …" is the main verb, not an aside.
